title: Grade 6 Science — Mon, Jun 09
description: Separation of Substances — Day 1 of 5: Why we separate and basic methods
subject: science

questions.question: A mixture is made of:
options: Two or more substances mixed together
Only one substance in pure form
questions.explanation: A mixture contains two or more substances mixed together. The substances can often be separated.

questions.question: Why do we need to separate mixtures?
options: To get useful substances and remove harmful ones
questions.explanation: We separate mixtures to get the useful part (e.g., clean water) or remove harmful substances (e.g., stones from rice).

questions.question: Picking out stones from rice by hand is an example of:
questions.explanation: Hand-picking is used to remove visible unwanted particles like stones or insects from food by hand.

questions.question: Winnowing is used to separate:
options: Heavy grains from light husk using wind
questions.explanation: Winnowing uses wind to blow away light husk while heavier grains fall and are collected.

questions.question: A sieve has small holes. It is used to separate:
questions.explanation: A sieve separates particles of different sizes — smaller ones fall through the holes; larger ones stay behind.

questions.question: Which method would you use to remove wheat flour from bran?
questions.explanation: Sieving is used to separate fine flour from coarser bran by passing through a fine mesh.

questions.question: A mixture of sand and stones can be separated by:
questions.explanation: Sand and stones differ in size, so sieving or hand-picking can separate them.

questions.question: Air is a mixture of:
options: Several gases including nitrogen, oxygen and others
questions.explanation: Air is a mixture of nitrogen (~78%), oxygen (~21%), carbon dioxide, and other gases.

questions.question: Which of these is a pure substance?
questions.explanation: Distilled water is pure — it has no dissolved salts or other substances mixed in.

questions.question: Farmers use winnowing in open fields because they need ____.
questions.explanation: Winnowing uses natural wind to blow away the lighter husk from heavier grain.

questions.question: Which of these is a mixture?
questions.explanation: Lemonade is a mixture of water, lemon juice, sugar, and salt — many substances together.

questions.question: Which method removes bigger impurities visible to the eye from grain?
questions.explanation: Hand-picking is the simplest method — you manually remove stones, insects, or other large impurities.

questions.question: A flour mill uses sieves to separate fine flour. The smaller the holes of the sieve:
options: The finer the flour that passes through
questions.explanation: Smaller holes in a sieve only allow finer particles through, producing finer flour.

questions.question: Seawater is a mixture of water and ____.
questions.explanation: Seawater contains water and many dissolved salts and minerals, making it a mixture.

questions.question: Which of these cannot be separated by hand-picking?
options: Pebbles from sand on a beach
questions.explanation: Salt dissolved in water cannot be picked by hand because it breaks into invisible ions. We need evaporation.
